threads.body: `getQueryText()` can throw `NoSuchElementException` if `getQueryTexts()` is empty (e.g., an empty `BatchStatement`). Even though this method is deprecated, it should be safe and return an empty string when no query texts are available.

`CassandraRequest.create(Session, String, boolean)` is deprecated in favor of `create(Session, String)`, but the replacement factory is currently package-private, so external callers cannot migrate off the deprecated API. Either make the replacement factory method(s) public, or adjust the deprecation guidance to point to an accessible alternative.

`create(Session, Statement<?>)` currently delegates to the deprecated `create(Session, String, boolean)` overload. Even though this is internal code, it can reintroduce deprecation warnings and is a bit confusing since the class already has a non-deprecated internal factory that takes a `Collection<String>`.

Consider calling the private `create(Session, Collection<String>, ...)` overload directly to avoid using the deprecated API internally.

`MultiQuery.Builder.add` accepts a `@Nullable` `queryText`, but the builder stores it into a `Set<String>` that is later joined into `db.query.text`. Since `SqlQueryAnalyzerUtil.analyzeWithSummary(...)` requires a non-null query text, allowing null here is misleading and could result in a literal "null" being appended if this builder is ever reused with nullable inputs. Tighten the contract by making `queryText` non-null (or explicitly normalizing null to "").

In this test class, other assertions expect NETWORK_TYPE to be absent when stable DB semconv is enabled (see earlier uses of `emitStableDatabaseSemconv() ? null : "ipv4"`). These new batch tests assert `NETWORK_TYPE == "ipv4"` unconditionally, which makes them inconsistent with the rest of the file and likely to fail under the stable-semconv configuration.

Align the expectation with the existing pattern in this test class.
